findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default, so `timezone.now()` is called exactly once when the module is first imported. Every `AssignmentSource` created afterwards (including all instances built by `from_integration`) carries the process-start timestamp instead of the time the assignment was actually queued. Any logging/debugging or future staleness check based on `queued` will be wrong, and `__eq__` (which includes `queued`) will differ between processes for otherwise identical sources. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: AssignmentSource does not survive a serialization round-trip through the task queue
findings.body: `to_dict()` (via `asdict`) puts a raw `datetime` into the dict that is passed as celery task kwargs in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`, and `from_dict()` just splats the dict into the constructor with no coercion. Depending on the configured task serializer this either (a) fails to serialize the task payload, breaking all outbound assignee syncs, or (b) round-trips `queued` as an ISO string, which `from_dict` happily accepts because dataclasses perform no type validation — leaving a field annotated `datetime` holding a `str`. Tests only exercise the eager/in-process path, so neither case is covered. Serialize `queued` explicitly (e.g. `isoformat()`) and parse it back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: from_dict silently returns None, disabling cycle protection
findings.body: When the payload is malformed, `from_dict` swallows the error and returns `None`. In `sync_assignee_outbound` a `None` source means `should_sync("outbound_assignee", None)` falls back to the old behaviour and the change is propagated back to the originating integration — i.e. the exact sync loop this PR is meant to break — with no log line or metric to indicate it happened. At minimum log a warning here so a serialization regression is detectable.

findings.title: `assignment_source` added to abstract sync_status_outbound but never passed or implemented
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` now declares `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`, but no caller passes it (the status-sync task is unchanged) and none of the concrete implementations (Jira, Jira Server, VSTS, Example, ...) were updated to accept or use it. The parameter is dead code that suggests inbound status webhooks are protected against sync cycles when they are not. Either wire the status path through (task -> `should_sync("outbound_status", source)` -> implementations) or drop the parameter.

findings.title: New `assignment_source` kwarg passed to duck-typed installations that may not accept it
findings.body: The task resolves `installation` by `hasattr(installation, "sync_assignee_outbound")` and now always passes `assignment_source=...`. The abstract declaration in `IssueSyncIntegration` was not updated to include this parameter, so it is only tolerated by implementations that happen to declare `**kwargs`. Any installation implementing `sync_assignee_outbound(self, external_issue, user, assign=True)` without `**kwargs` will raise `TypeError`, which is not in the task's `retry(exclude=...)` list and will therefore burn 5 retries for every assignment. Declare the parameter explicitly on the abstract method (and in the implementations) rather than relying on `**kwargs`.

findings.title: Task kwarg is always sent, breaking old workers during rollout
findings.body: `assignment_source_dict` is included in the `apply_async` kwargs unconditionally (as `None` when there is no source). During a rolling deploy, workers still running the previous revision of `sync_assignee_outbound` do not accept this keyword and the task will fail with `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument`, dropping assignee syncs for the duration of the rollout. Only include the key when `assignment_source` is not `None`.

findings.title: No test that a different integration's assignment source still syncs outbound
findings.body: The new tests cover source=None and source==the same integration, but not the case the PR explicitly claims to preserve: an assignment originating from integration A must still be propagated outbound to integration B. Since the guard in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` compares `sync_source.integration_id` to `org_integration.integration_id`, a mistake there (e.g. comparing against `org_integration.id`) would silently suppress all outbound syncs for every integration and no test would catch it. Add a case with two linked integrations where the source is one of them.
